text: spine ARCHITECTURE.md §10 cites apple-refs/reminders.png as the macOS 26 'What's New' onboarding pattern; that screenshot is the Reminders main window, not a What's New sheet — followed the written description instead

swift-argument-parser fills a command's positional arguments before it looks for a subcommand name, so a command with a positional cannot host subcommands — 'meetings transcript edit' needed an argv rewrite in the root command instead
gauntlet units share one worktree: 'git stash' to A/B a build stashed three other units' in-flight edits; recovered with stash pop, but build --target is the safe check

Parallel units share one worktree and one .build: swift test/build failed twice mid-run on another unit's half-saved file (NoteCommand.swift, CLISupport.swift), and verify.sh still fails on their in-flight AppSourceGuardTests.panelGlassIsNeverFaded — a per-unit scratch-path or worktree would make a unit's own verify trustworthy
swift 6.2.4 SILGen crashes (signal 5) on compactMap(\.configuration.commandName) over [ParsableCommand.Type]; an explicit for-loop compiles
MeetingsApp has no test target, so app-level regressions (markdown rendering, view predicates) can only be guarded by source-scanning tests inside MeetingsCoreTests
concurrent workers share one working tree: peers' half-finished edits in MeetingsApp/Tests broke my swift test runs; had to build an isolated rsync copy of MeetingsCore+Tests to measure anything
grep skips Sources/MeetingsCore/Store/MeetingStore.swift and two test files as 'binary' — they carry a literal NUL in a doc comment, so plain grep silently finds nothing; grep -a is needed
scripts/shot.sh: screencapture -l <wid> fails 'could not create image from window' while full-screen screencapture works; per-window capture unusable this session
swift test contends on the shared .build lock when several unit agents share one worktree; --scratch-path <dir> gives each agent its own build and unblocks
